title: Hash Maps & Sets
summary: Use sets for membership and maps for key/value information like counts.
refresher: A set answers “have I seen this?” A hash map answers “what value belongs to this key?” Counts, indexes, and grouped data often use maps.

sections.title: Sets answer membership questions
sections.summary: A set keeps one copy of each value.

blocks.body: Use a set when you only care whether a value has appeared. It is perfect for duplicate checks because lookup is fast and the code stays small.

blocks.caption: The second time a value appears, membership tells you it is a repeat.

blocks.prompt: Which structure is best for asking “have I seen this value before?”
blocks.why: A set stores unique values and gives a direct membership check.

sections.title: Maps connect keys to values
sections.summary: A map stores a value under a key.

blocks.body: Use a map when a value needs attached information. For example, a character can point to how many times it appears.

blocks.caption: A set can tell you a letter appeared. A map can tell you how many times.

blocks.prompt: Why use a map for an anagram check?
blocks.why: An anagram check needs matching character counts, not just membership.
